title: Company Operational Guardrails and Forms
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

Purpose
- This handbook consolidates company-wide operational guardrails, required approval flows, and reusable templates for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. It is intended to reduce ambiguity, accelerate approvals, and ensure consistent risk controls across Redwood Inference.

Scope
- Applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors accessing Redwood systems, procuring goods/services on Redwood’s behalf, or handling Redwood data.

Owner & Contacts
- Document owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team).
- Primary contact: Aisha Patel (Finance Operations).
- Security contact for access/data questions: Daniel Kim (Security).
- Procurement contact: Marcus Nguyen (Finance).

1) Access & Permissions

Principles
- Least privilege by default: grant the minimal permissions required for a role and justify any permanent elevation.
- Role-based provisioning: access should be requested via role templates where possible.
- Time-bound elevations: temporary access must have an explicit expiry.

Systems and tools (examples)
- Identity provider: Okta (SSO, SCIM provisioning).
- Ticketing & approvals: Jira Service Management (Access Requests queue).
- Admin audit logs: Confluence pages and centralized audit store (retention policy below).

Access request workflow (standard)
1. Employee opens an Access Request (Jira) and selects the relevant role template.
2. Manager approves (auto-sends to system owner if role is sensitive).
3. System owner (service owner) reviews and approves. For high-privilege roles, Security review is required.
4. Provisioning is completed via automated SCIM; the ticket updates automatically and closes on completion.

Approval matrix (summary)
- Low-risk roles (view-only, non-sensitive data): manager approval.
- Mid-risk roles (write access to internal services, moderate data): manager + service owner.
- High-risk roles (admin, PII systems, production infra): manager + service owner + security.

Access reviews and cadence
- Quarterly automated access reviews for all groups.
- Ad-hoc reviews triggered by org changes, incidents, or M&A.

Emergency access (break-glass)
- Break-glass requests must be raised via the emergency access form in Jira and receive two verbal approvals (on-call SRE + service owner); logged and reviewed post-event within 72 hours.

2) Change Management

Change tiers and requirements
- Tier 0 (Standard non-disruptive): e.g., documentation updates, config flags with no production impact. Approval: owner.
- Tier 1 (Low-risk): deployment with no schema changes, non-breaking feature flags. Approval: owner + release manager.
- Tier 2 (High-risk): infra changes, database migrations, model-serving changes likely to affect latency or cost. Approval: owner + release manager + SRE + Security if applicable.
- Tier 3 (Critical): customer-facing outage risk or data migration with rollback implications. Requires formal change review board (CRB) sign-off.

Change window and scheduling
- Standard deployment windows: weekdays 10:00–17:00 local PST. High-risk changes should be scheduled during agreed maintenance windows and communicated 72 hours in advance.

Change submission checklist (required fields)
- Change title, owner, impact summary, rollback plan, test & verification steps, monitoring playbook, scheduled window, and stakeholders.

Rollback & validation
- Every Tier 2+ change must include: clear rollback steps, automated smoke tests, canary plan, and metrics to validate success. Post-change review within 3 business days.

3) Data Management

Data classification levels
- Public: no restrictions.
- Internal: business data not regulated.
- Confidential: internal product or customer information requiring encryption at rest and in transit.
- Restricted/PII: highly sensitive data subject to legal/regulatory controls.

Storage & handling rules
- Restricted/PII must be stored only in approved systems with encryption (KMS-backed).
- No Restricted/PII in public cloud storage buckets without lifecycle and ACL controls.
- Developers must use anonymized datasets for dev environments; production data access requires documented justification and a time-bound approval.

Retention & deletion
- Default retention: Internal data 3 years, Confidential 7 years, Restricted as per contract/regulation.
- Data deletion requests: route through Data Governance (Jira) with owner sign-off.

Backups & recovery
- Critical datasets must have 7-day hot backups and 30-day cold backups. Recovery RTO targets are documented on a per-service basis in runbooks.

Data incident response
- Suspected data exposure must follow Security Incident Response runbook: notify Security within 1 hour, preserve logs, and escalate to Legal if required.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Procurement thresholds and authority
- Low-value purchases (< $2,500): team lead approval.
- Mid-value ($2,500–$50,000): procurement team + Finance approval.
- High-value (> $50,000): Director+ approval and Legal review for contracts.

Preferred vendors & framework agreements
- Finance maintains preferred vendor list for cloud, hardware, travel, and recruiting. Use preferred vendors when available to leverage volume discounts and pre-approved contract terms.

Purchase process (summary)
1. Complete a Purchase Request in Procurement system (link provided in Slack #procurement).
2. Attach vendor quote, business justification, and budget code.
3. Procurement validates vendor, issues PO, and tracks delivery.
4. Finance processes invoices via NetSuite/Coupa (system depends on your team).

Expense reimbursements
- Employees submit expenses within 30 days via expense system (Ramp/Concur). Receipts required for items > $25. Per diem rates follow table in Appendix. Non-compliant claims will be rejected and sent back to the submitter.

Capital vs. Opex classification
- Procurement determines capital treatment for purchases > $5,000 with Finance. Requestors should indicate potential capitalization in the purchase request.

5) Vendor Management

Vendor onboarding checklist
- Risk assessment (vendor questionnaire and security self-attestation).
- Legal review of contract terms (data residency, liability, termination, SLAs).
- Finance set up for payments and 1099/contractor classification.
- Technical onboarding: API keys, IP allowlists, test environment access.

Security & privacy requirements
- Vendors handling Restricted/PII require SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) and an executed Data Processing Addendum (DPA).
- Where vendor does not meet certification, compensating controls and written risk acceptance by Security & Legal are required.

Vendor risk tiers
- Tier A (Strategic/high risk): Vendors with production infra, customer data, or integrated billing. Quarterly reviews and 24-hour incident notification requirement.
- Tier B (Moderate): Non-critical SaaS with limited data. Semi-annual reviews.
- Tier C (Low-risk): Office supplies, ad hoc consultants. Annual reviews.

Offboarding
- Revoke credentials, remove API keys, terminate accounts, and verify data return/destruction per contract within 30 days.

6) Travel Policy

Booking & approvals
- Employees should use the company travel portal (preferred travel vendor) for bookings.
- Domestic travel < $1,000: manager approval. International or premium class travel: departmental head approval + Finance pre-clearance.

Per diem and allowable expenses
- Lodging: reasonable and mid-market; receipts required.
- Meals: per diem set regionally (see Appendix table). Alcohol OK when compliant with local law and business context; must be reasonable.
- Ground transportation: preferred ride-share or company car rental. Receipts required.

Safety & emergency
- Employees traveling for business must register travel in the company travel tracker and have emergency contact info in HR. For travel advisories, consult People Ops.

7) Templates & Appendices

Included templates (copy-and-use)
- Access Request Template (form fields): requester, manager, role, justification, expiry date, systems affected.
- Change Request Template: title, owner, risk tier, impact, rollback plan, test steps, monitoring metrics.
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist: vendor info, certifications, contract owner, payment terms, technical contacts.
- Procurement Request Form: vendor, SOW/quote, budget code, business justification, expected deliverables.

Appendix: Example Approval Matrix (table text)
- Manager only: low-cost software subscriptions, non-sensitive tooling.
- Manager + Procurement: cloud credits, equipment up to $50k.
- Director + Legal: high-value contracts, strategic platform agreements.

Appendix: Retention Table (text)
- Public: retain as needed.
- Internal: 3 years.
- Confidential: 7 years.
- Restricted: per contract/regulation.

Monitoring & Compliance
- Regular audits: Finance & Security run cross-functional audits twice a year to confirm compliance with procurement approvals, vendor SLAs, access reviews, and data retention.
- Exceptions: documented via the Risk & Exceptions process and require owner_team + Legal approval.

Change history and maintenance
- This handbook is reviewed annually. Emergency updates can be made by the document owner with reviewers notified.

Key links and references

Contact and escalation

- For access or data handling questions: security@redwood.ai
- For travel assistance: people-ops@redwood.ai

End of document.
